main_issue: Whether and how Agent D can keep cooking strong-smelling devil curry in the shared flat given the smell affecting others' calls, rooms and laundry

A-B.evidence: A asked for no strong-smelling food (T1); B first said the day doesn't matter (T8), then accepted once-weekly Saturday cooking with window open (T14, T18), which fits A's Saturday arrangement.

A-C.evidence: C complained about smell (T3) and said the day doesn't matter (T9), then said opening the window would work (T15), accepting the arrangement A helped set up.

A-D.evidence: A asked for no strong-smelling cooking (T1), proposed Saturday (T5); D agreed (T6), then agreed to once weekly and window open (T13, T16); A thanked D (T7).

B-C.evidence: C: 'She's right. The day doesn't matter for my laundry either' (T9); C backs B's window solution (T15).

B-D.evidence: B rejected the Saturday and notification fixes (T8, T12); D offered once a week (T13), B proposed window open and door shut (T14), D agreed (T16), B thanked (T18).

C-D.evidence: C said the day doesn't matter (T9); D offered notice, once a week; C said an open window works (T15); D agreed to open the window (T16).
